body.text: What time of morning do you need to arrive at Kaputaş Beach for parking and sunbeds?

Reach Kaputaş Beach by 08:15–08:30 between June and September if you want a legal pull-off space along the D400 highway and a front-row municipal sunbed. By 10:00, roadside bays stretch several hundred metres toward Kalkan, and the narrow shingle shore fills rapidly with swimmers arriving from both Kaş and Kalkan.

Kaputaş sits in a steep gorge roughly 20 kilometres west of Kaş and 10 kilometres east of Kalkan, as noted by [GoTürkiye Antalya](https://goturkiye.com/antalya/touch). Because it is a First Degree Natural Protected Area with no dedicated multi-storey car park, cars line the cliffside highway shoulder. Arriving early also gives you calmer water before afternoon Mediterranean swells pick up and churn the fine shingle near the shoreline.
How many stairs lead down to the cove (187 steps)?

Exactly 187 concrete steps connect the D400 coastal road to the shingle and sand floor of Kaputaş Gorge. The staircase is wide and fitted with handrails, making the walk down straightforward in the morning, though the climb back up in midday heat demands steady pacing, drinking water, and proper footwear rather than thin flip-flops.

There is no lift or ramp into the cove, so travellers carrying beach bags, umbrellas, or young children should pack light. [GoTürkiye’s Kaputaş guide](https://goturkiye.com/blog/kaputas-beach) highlights the dramatic canyon backdrop and clear water, but the cove offers minimal natural shade until late afternoon when the western cliff blocks direct sun. A municipal café at beach level rents loungers and umbrellas and provides basic showers and changing cabins, though queues build fast after 10:30.
How does Kaputaş compare to Patara's 18-km sand beach?

Kaputaş is a compact, steep-walled turquoise cove built for a focused two-hour morning swim, whereas Patara stretches across 18 kilometres of open golden sand backed by wind-sculpted dunes and ancient Lycian ruins. Kaputaş rewards early arrival and dramatic cliff photos; Patara offers space, shallow entry, and afternoon breezes without feeling boxed in.

body.text: According to [GoTürkiye Patara](https://goturkiye.com/patara/see), Patara is Türkiye’s longest beach and a Special Environmental Protection Zone for loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta). Between May and September, visitors must leave the beach before dusk so nesting mothers and hatchlings remain undisturbed. Check seasonal site hours—08:30–19:00 in summer and 08:30–17:30 in winter—on [Turkish Museums](https://www.turkishmuseums.com/museum/detail/1968-antalya-patara/1968/4).
Can you combine both on a Kaş–Fethiye drive?

Yes—combining Kaputaş and Patara works smoothly on a single Kaş–Fethiye transfer or self-drive day if you swim at Kaputaş first and visit Patara after midday. Driving from Kaş to Kaputaş takes about 20 minutes, Patara lies another 30 minutes west via Kalkan, and Fethiye sits roughly 75–90 minutes beyond Patara.
A practical Kaş-to-Fethiye checklist keeps the day unhurried:

items: Depart Kaş by 07:45 to park at Kaputaş before the 09:00 rush.
Pack water shoes, reef-safe sunscreen, and a dry bag for the 187 steps.
Stop in Kalkan or Gelemiş village for a shaded lunch before entering Patara.
Walk the restored Lycian League Parliament and Triumphal Arch at Patara before heading onto the sand.
Leave the Patara dunes 30 minutes before turtle-protection closure if continuing to Fethiye before dark.

faq.q: What is the best month to visit Kaputaş Beach?
faq.a: Late May, June, and September offer warm swimming water with lighter D400 roadside parking pressure than July and August. Early morning arrival still matters in shoulder months on weekends.

faq.q: Is there an entrance fee for Kaputaş Beach in 2026?
faq.a: Kaputaş operates as a municipal beach with modest local charges for entry or sunbed and umbrella rental, payable by card or Turkish lira. Rates adjust seasonally, so carry a small amount of cash as backup.

faq.q: Does the Patara Ancient City ticket include Patara Beach?
faq.a: Yes. One €15 e-ticket from the Ministry of Culture and Tourism covers both the Patara archaeological ruins and road access through the site to the main beach car park.

faq.q: Can you reach Kaputaş Beach without a rental car?
faq.a: Yes. Regular dolmuş minibuses run along the D400 between Kaş and Kalkan every 20–30 minutes in summer and drop passengers right beside the top of the 187 steps.

faq.q: Why does Patara Beach close in the evening?
faq.a: Patara is a protected Caretta caretta loggerhead sea turtle nesting beach. Evening closure keeps the sand dark and quiet so adult turtles can lay eggs and hatchlings can navigate toward the sea.

faq.q: Are the 187 steps at Kaputaş safe for young children or older travellers?
faq.a: The concrete steps have handrails and even risers, so active children and mobile adults manage them fine at a slow pace. Strollers and travellers with knee or mobility limits will find Patara’s flat boardwalk far easier.
